jess: Heads-up — starting onboarding for trident-7b (from thirdparty repo). Legal flagged a clause that might affect us: 'no commercial redistribution of model weights' and an attribution requirement. Can someone confirm whether we can serve quantized weights in Dedicated/Private? :thinking:

michael: Put the exact snippet? sometimes 'no redistribution' only applies to public rehosting, not serving from infra. :eyes:

jess: Here — copied license excerpt: ```
Redistribution: The rights to copy, modify, and redistribute the model weights are granted for non-commercial research only. Commercial redistribution is prohibited. Attribution: Any use in a product must include attribution to Original Authors and link to LICENSE.```

michael: Thanks. Short answer: serving via API (hosted or dedicated) typically doesn't count as 'redistribution' so long as we don't publish the raw quantized files. But the wording is ambiguous — depends on 'redistribute' definition. I'll escalate to legal for written opinion.

sarah: From ML side: we already ran baseline quant experiments (4-bit GPTQ) on a dev node. Performance: MMLU down ~1.8 pts at 4-bit, perplexity +6% on thin eval set. Latency improvements ~2.4x. If legal says serving is ok, we can provide a quantized variant behind Dedicated-only routes.

arjun: Ops concern: even if legal signs off, customers sometimes expect to download optimized weights (we should block that). For Dedicated/private we can restrict export. Need to validate backups and artifact retention so we never persist an accessible tarball.

liz: On attribution: the license wants link + author. For UI/legal copy we can add small footer in docs and a mandatory metadata header in provenance logs. Is that sufficient for the clause?

michael: If it's just attribution, yes—docs + provenance logs + an internal record should satisfy it. But the 'commercial redistribution' bit is the blocker. I asked legal to confirm by EOD and flagged the model for 'redistrib-review'.

jess: Two follow-ups for ML/QA while we wait: 1) Sarah — can you run the standard eval suite (MMLU, HellaSwag, Rouge) on the 4-bit build and attach diffs? 2) Arjun — add a policy check in the upload pipeline to block artifact export if license=restrictive.

sarah: Will do. Quick note: initial evals show a regression in conversational safety classifiers — FPR up 0.7%. I'll run prompt-level regression tests to see if it's systematic. Also prepping a perf/quality matrix to decide if we should keep quantized variant in rolling canary.

arjun: I'll stub the upload-policy hook today. We can have a hard fail when an upload has "redistribution": "prohibited" in metadata. Works with current ingestion.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch "trident/quant-eval" to staging (gpu-small-1) — logs at https://ci.example/builds/6789 :rocket:

jess: Thanks. michael — ping legal update here when they respond. If legal approves 'serve-only' we want a short-run plan: canary to internal customers, enable Dedicated only, no raw weights export, add attribution strings and provenance header.

michael: Legal wrote back (copied text): "Serving model outputs via API is allowed under license so long as the model weights are not redistributed. Customer-provided hosting (where customer fully controls weight binaries) may be restricted. Attribution is required in product documentation." :thumbsup:

jess: Great, that's the green light we needed. Action items: Sarah (run full eval + attach diffs), Arjun (implement upload-policy + audit logs), Liz (create attribution copy & provenance header format), Michael (store legal memo in compliance tracker). I'll open a short RFC for the canary plan once we have eval results.

sarah: Uploaded results: https://artifacts.internal/trident-7b/quant-eval-2026-03-21.csv — MMLU: base 62.3 vs 4-bit 60.5, HellaSwag 86.1 -> 85.0, Rouge-L on summarization -1.5. Safety classifier FPR +0.7. I'll add more prompt-set analysis.

arjun: Upload-policy PR: https://git.internal/p/infra/pipeline/+/234 — adds metadata check and a block on artifact-download unless role=security or role=compliance.

liz: Attribution proposal posted in #docs: "Trident-7b — model by Trident Research Initiative. Licensed under TRIL-1. See LICENSE for details." Also added machine-readable provenance header: `X-Model-Origin: trident-7b;license=TRIL-1;quantized=true;date=2026-03-21`.

jess: Perfect. Leaving this thread open until canary RFC is live. Thanks everyone. :party_popper:
